name: Strontium titanate
equilibrium_context: Quantum paraelectric, centrosymmetric at all temperatures, no ferroelectricity in equilibrium; antiferrodistortive transition at 105 K
summary: The most prominent and most fiercely contested case in the field. Four states, two of them contested.

driven_states.emergent_property: Excitation of the highest-frequency A2u mode in the mid-infrared produces a non-centrosymmetric polar phase with polarization along [1-10], demonstrated by time-delay-independent second harmonic generation. A low-frequency polar mode hardens as the signal grows, as in a para-ferroelectric transition.
driven_states.source: Nova, Disa, Fechner & Cavalleri, Science 364, 1075 (2019), doi:10.1126/science.aaw4911
driven_states.caveat: Not a single-pulse effect, but a cumulative transformation over tens of thousands of pulses. The authors themselves explain the domain structure photoflexoelectrically (two oppositely oriented domains, no monodomain state) and invoke pre-existing polar nanoregions. The evidence is optical plus capacitively coupled current pulses; there is no direct measurement of a remanent macroscopic polarization and no hysteresis curve. The observation is robust, the label ferroelectricity is not.

threshold.quantity: accumulation, saturation after about 1e4 to 1e5 pulses at 1 kHz

further_sources: Fechner et al., Nature Materials (2024), doi:10.1038/s41563-023-01791-y (X-ray diffuse scattering: quenching of octahedral rotation fluctuations)
Libbi, Monacelli & Kozinsky, Nat. Commun. 17, 6699 (2026), doi:10.1038/s41467-026-72675-3 (theory)

driven_states.emergent_property: A single intense THz cycle drives the ferroelectric soft mode ionically along the pathway into the positions of a new, symmetry-broken structure. The symmetry lowering shows up in markedly altered phonon spectra.
driven_states.source: Li, Qiu, Zhang, Baldini, Lu, Rappe & Nelson, Science 364, 1079 (2019), doi:10.1126/science.aaw4913
driven_states.caveat: Despite the title, the state is purely transient (about 10 ps) and therefore not a metastable state. The evidence is indirect, via phonon spectra and second harmonic generation. Cheng et al. show for KTaO3 that long-lived second harmonic signals can also originate from defect-induced local polar structures, which bears back on this class of experiments.

threshold.quantity: nonlinear rise above about 200 to 300 kV/cm

further_sources: Cheng et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 130, 126902 (2023), doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.130.126902 (control test on KTaO3)

driven_states.emergent_property: Resonant driving of the infrared-active soft mode with a circularly polarised THz field produces a circulating ionic motion and thereby a magnetization along the rotation axis - dynamical multiferroicity.

drive.driven_mode: infrared-active polar soft mode, circularly excited

driven_states.source: Basini, Pancaldi, Wehinger et al., Nature 628, 534 (2024), doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07175-9
driven_states.caveat: Not an ordered state, but a driven magnetization; the signal disappears with the pulse. Attributing the Kerr signal to a genuine magnetization rather than to a non-magnetic optical artifact is the critical point of the work and has so far been shown by one group.

threshold.quantity: no threshold, quadratic scaling with the field amplitude

driven_states.emergent_property: The lowest-frequency optical phonon mode is driven far into the anharmonic regime; energy is transferred nonlinearly to higher-frequency modes. The ionic displacements are imaged directly with femtosecond X-ray pulses.

drive.driven_mode: TO1 soft mode, coupling to modes between 5 and 15 THz

driven_states.source: Kozina, Fechner, Marsik et al., Nature Physics 15, 387 (2019), doi:10.1038/s41567-018-0408-1
driven_states.caveat: Purely a lattice state, no new electronic or polar order. The entry documents the driving mechanism underlying the ferroelectricity entries and is therefore methodologically relevant, not as a material state in its own right.

threshold.quantity: upconversion sets in above the harmonic displacement amplitude

sources: Kozina et al., Nature Physics 15, 387 (2019), doi:10.1038/s41567-018-0408-1
gaps: The dispute is not settled: Fechner et al. 2024 support the ferroelectricity reading microscopically, while the KTaO3 control test and the defect explanations argue against it.

Nature Physics work from 2025 shows that the equilibrium material itself is more inhomogeneous than assumed - this complicates separating light-generated order from light-aligned pre-existing polar nanoregions.
